title: Harvard plate tests favor one HD 303514 recovery state over one eclipse-loss state
abstract: Two published HD 303514 states fitted TESS and ASAS-3 data but predict different eclipse histories. We test their single best training states on 2,855 DASCH DR7 plate measurements from 1889 to 1955. A common IAS15 solver gives weighted fit gains of 88.34 for the recovery state and 53.49 for the loss state, with one free amplitude and separate plate-series offsets. Common-shape templates that test timing alone give 82.54 and 66.39. Every tested plate cut and each of three eras favors the recovery state. The native finite-step loss-state solver gives gains of 53.21 and 66.70, so its numerical timing error does not change the ranking. This is a fixed-state comparison. No orbital fit to plates or probability of eclipse loss is claimed. Plate calibration, error correlations, twin-star assumptions and unsearched orbital branches limit the result. Code, fitted states, aggregate evidence and an external-data retrieval script are included.

display.caption: Predicted primary separation, held-out plate fit gain against time shift, and model preference under plate cuts. The gain is a weighted residual statistic, not calibrated evidence odds. Timing uses the same eclipse shape for both states.
